record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the linked full paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README presents a multi-direction ablation method for suppressing refusals and reports its attack success rates. It does not report a controlled test of the claim versions; the README's qualitative comparison with a single-direction baseline has no baseline results to inspect.
record.gate_note: The README reports per-model attack success rates for the authors' multi-direction ablation configurations. It states that the method outperforms a single-direction baseline, but does not give the baseline values. Figure descriptions provide no extractable numerical results.
record.test_reason: The study argues and reports that refusal is a manifold of several related directions. It says ablating several SOM-derived directions beats the single difference-in-means baseline, which bears on V4. Only the README was available: it states the comparison but gives no baseline numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude that refusal is a low-dimensional manifold captured by several closely related directions. Ablating a BO-selected set of SOM-derived directions suppresses refusal better than the single difference-in-means direction and specialized jailbreaks. They also say SOMs provably generalize difference-in-means.
record.recipe_differences: Tool/attack repository using SOM-derived multiple directions and Bayesian optimization to select directions for ablation, rather than the original single difference-in-means direction. README gives no numerical single-direction comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported attack success rates differ across the listed model configurations; the README does not give results for alternative settings under the same model.

fits_no_version.finding: As more directions are ablated, the harmful-prompt cluster moves toward the harmless one and becomes more compact. Authors say this compaction correlates strongly with ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal suppression correlates with compaction of the harmful representation cluster under multi-direction ablation.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, as stated in the README citation.
record.problems: The README supplies no single-direction baseline values, uncertainty estimates, or capability-retention results. The reported rates are repository README claims; the code and linked paper were not inspected or run.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numerical results were left out. Qualitative figure descriptions and the unquantified statement that the method outperforms the single-direction baseline were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: README gives no single-direction ablation ASR, no induction-by-addition result and no capability retention. It only says the single direction is outperformed.
No weight-edit abliteration of released models reported.
README compares with jailbreak algorithms only in ASR terms. It does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, and reports no adversarial training.
Not tested. Mistral-7B-RR's low ASR is not analysed as a training effect in the README.

missing.what: Single-direction (difference-in-means) baseline ASR per model, and jailbreak-baseline ASRs, needed to quantify the multi vs. single comparison.
missing.locator: Full paper arXiv:2511.08379, main results table (not in README)

missing.what: ASR as a function of number of ablated directions, plus the cosine similarity among SOM directions.
missing.locator: README Mechanistic Analysis figures; paper figures

missing.what: Any capability or utility retention measurements after multi-direction ablation.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available. The V4 verdict rests on the authors' unquantified statement and should be revisited against the paper's tables. Mistral-7B-RR (circuit breakers) reaches only 25.79% ASR, notably lower than the other models. This may bear on V3/V7 robustness, but no baseline or analysis is given. Ablation here is still of directions inspired by and generalizing Arditi et al., so the study builds on V1 while arguing it is incomplete.

versions.untested_parts: Whether ablating the original difference-in-means direction removes refusal, whether adding it induces harmless refusals, and whether other abilities are retained.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No test of whether other jailbreaks suppress the single refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The README asserts that multiple directions outperform a single-direction baseline, but gives no baseline results or comparative measurements to evaluate that claim.
No measurement separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct stages is reported.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.

They state that multi-direction ablation outperforms the single-direction baseline. That is an argument plus a stated result that the single-direction account needs restating, so T5 fits (T2 is also defensible). The reader's earlier T4 is wrong: the text states a comparison with the single-direction baseline.
